title: G01.5 generic text provider and Cockpit migration
description: Decouple active G01 pre-production text stages from 9Router through a small provider-neutral TextProvider contract and a Cockpit OpenAI-compatible adapter.
businessContext: Creators use a locally configured Cockpit server for text generation. New pre-production projects must use verified text capability without a 9Router credential or certification.
acceptanceCriteria: Active G01 text stages depend on a small generic TextProvider abstraction, not NineRouterClient or provider endpoint details.

CockpitTextProvider safely normalizes configured base URLs and uses OpenAI-compatible /responses and /models with bearer authentication, timeout/abort support, defensive response parsing, and normalized safe errors.
Provider-neutral settings persist Cockpit base URL, selected model, and only a secret reference; old 9Router settings are retained as legacy and are never copied into Cockpit credentials.
Creator-facing configuration shows provider-neutral text capability, configured-secret state, test connection, refresh models, and no active 9Router certification instruction.
Structured generation centrally extracts text, parses JSON, validates supplied schemas, and returns normalized parse/validation errors without weakening stage schemas.
Deterministic provider, persistence/configuration, renderer/provider-settings, and representative G01 workflow integration tests cover required success and failure cases.
Typecheck, lint, desktop build, targeted tests, and broader unit tests pass; no G02+ action/progress runtime or media/CapCut redesign is implemented.
humanEscalationConditions: Cockpit API behavior differs from the documented OpenAI-compatible models or responses contracts.
A secure credential migration would need to read, copy, or reinterpret an existing 9Router secret.
An active G01 text stage cannot be migrated without changing G02+ action/progress architecture.
Latest-main baseline verification fails in an unrelated area.
